screening_decisions.reason: RCT of women with stress urinary incontinence. Intervention arms include PFM exercises (digital palpation and biofeedback); a no-exercise control arm is present. Meets population (SUI), intervention (PFMT), and comparator (no treatment).

RCT in women with SUI. App-based PFMT is the intervention; the control group received postponed treatment (wait-list, i.e., no active treatment during study). Criteria met (SUI, PFMT, inactive control).
RCT in postmenopausal women with SUI. PFME alone arm (PFMT) compared with a control group that received no active treatment. Satisfies all selection criteria.

RCT in women with urge/mixed UI. Behavioral treatment (biofeedback-assisted) is very likely to include PFMT as a core component; the study includes a placebo control arm, which is an inactive comparator. Because the abstract does not explicitly state PFMT, include conservatively.
RCT in older women with stress incontinence. Pelvic muscle exercise (PFMT) arm compared with a no-treatment control group. All criteria satisfied.
RCT in women with urodynamically proven stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises (PFMT) arm versus an untreated control group. Meets all criteria.
Randomized experimental study in women with SUI. Intervention group received perineal (pelvic floor) exercises; control group received no treatment. PFMT vs inactive control in SUI population.
RCT in women with urodynamic SUI. Pelvic floor exercises (PFMT) arm compared with an untreated control arm. Selection criteria fully met.
RCT in women with stress and mixed UI. PFMT group compared with a control group (no PFMT). Population (SUI/MUI), intervention (PFMT), and inactive comparator present.

RCT in adult women with UI (likely including SUI/UUI/MUI, though type not explicitly limited). Intervention includes BMP that incorporates pelvic floor muscle training (strength outcomes measured). Control group received no treatment. Include given presence of PFMT and inactive control.

Prospective randomized study in stress incontinence, but the abstract does not mention a no-treatment, placebo, sham, or inactive control arm. It compares medical gymnastics with electrical stimulation only. Does not meet comparator criterion.
RCT (crossover design) in elderly women with SUI. Multidimensional exercises include PFM training; control group received no exercise. PFMT vs inactive control, eligible.
RCT in women with stress, urge, and mixed UI. Exercise-only arm includes PFMT; education-only arm serves as an inactive control. Meets all criteria.
RCT in women with stress, urge, and mixed UI. Multidimensional exercise intervention includes PFMT; control group received no active treatment. Criteria satisfied.

Randomized controlled trial in older women with stress, urge, or mixed UI. Intervention includes pelvic floor muscle training and behavioural therapy; control group received advice/pamphlet only (inactive control). Fully eligible.
RCT in women with SUI. Treatment group received supervised PFMT; control group received no treatment. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized single-blind study in women with mild-to-moderate SUI. The Knack (timed PFM contraction) is a form of PFMT; wait-list control is an inactive comparator. Eligible.
RCT in women with SUI. Both individual and group PFMT arms are compared with a control group that received no treatment. Fully meets criteria.
RCT in women with MUI. PFMT arm is compared with a waiting-list control (inactive). Population, intervention, and comparator all satisfy inclusion.

RCT in postmenopausal women with UI (type unspecified but likely stress/mixed). Physical therapy includes PFMT; osteoporosis education control is an inactive comparator. Include based on presence of PFMT and inactive control.
RCT in women with UI. Pelvic muscle exercise (PFMT) arm is compared with bladder training and a control group (presumably no treatment). PFMT versus inactive control, eligible.
Randomized experimental study in women with SUI. Kinesitherapy (PFMT) arm and a control group with no treatment. Meets all criteria.
Randomized study in female volleyball athletes with SUI. PFMRP (PFMT programme) compared with a control group receiving only a pamphlet (inactive control). Eligible.
RCT in women with genuine stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises arm compared with a no-treatment control group. Meets criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in women with genuine stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises versus no therapy. All criteria satisfied.
RCT in women with stress/mixed UI; PFMT arm with pelvic floor exercises vs untreated control (no contact). Meets all criteria.

RCT protocol evaluating nurse specialist availability vs usual care; intervention is not PFMT (may include PFMT as part of usual advice but not the defined intervention). Does not meet PFMT arm criterion.
Not an RCT of PFMT; reports satisfaction outcomes from a nurse specialist trial. Does not meet study design or PFMT criterion.
RCT in women with urge/mixed UI; behavioral training arm includes PFMT (biofeedback for pelvic floor control) compared with self-help booklet (inactive control). Meets criteria.
Feasibility study, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet study design criterion.
RCT comparing two PFMT delivery modes (supervised vs unsupervised); both arms receive active PFMT. No inactive control arm.
RCT in women with stress UI, but control arm receives routine physiotherapy (active treatment). Not an inactive control.
RCT in women with stress/mixed UI; PFMT is part of behavioral training arms, self-help booklet is inactive control. Meets criteria.
RCT in elderly women with UI; intervention includes Kegel's exercises (PFMT) plus other exercises; control appears to be no intervention. Meets criteria.
RCT in women with UI; behavioral therapy arm likely includes PFMT (standard first-line behavioral treatment), control is no therapy. Conservatively include.
Economic evaluation alongside an RCT, not an original randomized trial. Does not meet study design criterion.
RCT comparing internet-based PFMT vs postal PFMT; both arms are active PFMT, no inactive control arm.
Long-term follow-up of a trial comparing two active PFMT delivery methods; no inactive control arm.
RCT in women with SUI; PFM co-contraction exercise arm vs control group (no exercise). Meets criteria.
Pilot RCT in frail older women with UI; behavioral treatments likely include PFMT, control no intervention. Conservatively include.
RCT in gynecologic cancer survivors; population not limited to women with stress, urge, or mixed UI (may have other pelvic floor dysfunction). Does not meet population criterion.
Questionnaire development and psychometric evaluation study, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criterion.
Systematic review of RCTs, not an original randomized trial. Does not meet study design criterion.
Systematic review of RCTs, not an original randomized trial. Does not meet study design criterion.
Methodological guidance on reporting trials, not a clinical trial itself. Does not meet study design criterion.
Narrative review/discussion article, not a randomized trial. Does not meet study design criterion.
Psychometric validation study of a quality of life questionnaire, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criterion.
Development and reproducibility testing of instruments, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criterion.
Observational MRI study of pelvic floor muscle function, not a randomized trial. Does not meet study design criterion.
Narrative review discussing mechanisms of PFMT, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criterion.
This is a terminology consensus report (IUGA/ICS joint report), not a randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trial. It does not evaluate an intervention.
This is a secondary analysis of a cross-sectional internet survey (EpiLUTS) in men and women, not an intervention trial. No PFMT arm.
This is a book chapter reviewing pharmacology of the lower urinary tract, not an original trial. No PFMT comparison.
This is a narrative review discussing optimal PFMT regimens; it is not an original RCT. No primary data.
This is a descriptive article on functional electrical stimulation (FES) for bladder inhibition, not a randomized trial of PFMT.
This is a secondary analysis of pelvic muscle resting pressures in healthy women (not UI), not an RCT of PFMT for incontinence.
This is a methodological guideline (GRADE) on preparing summary of findings tables, not a clinical trial.
This is a GRADE guideline on continuous outcomes in SoF tables, not a primary study of PFMT.
This is a community-based epidemiological survey (EPINCONT) assessing prevalence of UI, not an RCT. No intervention comparison.
This is a terminology consensus report for female pelvic floor dysfunction, not an intervention trial.
This is a methodological discussion about quality of interventions in systematic reviews, not an RCT.
This is a cross-sectional quality-of-life study using the Sickness Impact Profile in women attending an incontinence clinic. It is not a randomized trial.
This is a systematic review and economic modelling study of non-surgical treatments for SUI, not an original RCT.
This is a psychometric validation study of a urinary symptom questionnaire (BFLUTS), not an intervention trial.
This is a willingness-to-pay survey among patients with urge/mixed incontinence, not a randomized trial of PFMT.
This is a cross-sectional analysis of survey data (National Survey of Self-Care and Aging) examining association of UI with self-rated health, not an RCT.
This is the design and validation of a quality-of-life questionnaire for incontinent women, not an intervention trial.

This is a validation study of the York Incontinence Perceptions Scale, using data from a behavioral/educational RCT. The article itself reports scale properties, not efficacy outcomes of PFMT. Furthermore, the intervention was a behavioral/educational program, not explicitly PFMT. Exclude.
This is a content validity study of the King's Health Questionnaire in OAB patients, not an intervention trial.
This is a methodological meta-research study examining the impact of trial quality on meta-analysis estimates, not a primary RCT.
This is the CONSORT reporting guideline for randomized trials, not a trial itself.
This is a cross-sectional survey assessing bothersomeness and QoL of UI in four European countries, not an RCT.
This is a descriptive study of pelvic muscle activity in nulliparous healthy continent women, not a trial in incontinent women and not an intervention study.
This is a validation of a severity index for epidemiological surveys, comparing with pad-weighing tests; not an intervention trial.
This is a cross-sectional study comparing female sexual function between incontinent and continent women, not an RCT.
Not a randomised or quasi-randomised trial. This is a prospective cohort study examining responsiveness of a self-efficacy index.
Not a trial; this article describes development of short-form questionnaires (IIQ and UDI).
Not a trial; this is a development and validation study of the I-QOL questionnaire.
Not a UI study; it validates the QOLS-N in psoriasis patients. Also not a trial of PFMT.
Not a trial of PFMT vs inactive control. This is a secondary analysis of duloxetine RCTs, validating global impression questions.
Not a trial; this describes the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale development. No PFMT.

RCT in women with stress incontinence. Intervention: pelvic floor muscle exercise training. Control group (n=27) likely received no active treatment, consistent with an inactive control. Study compares PFMT vs control.

RCT in women with stress urinary incontinence comparing three arms: PFMT+electrotherapy, PFMT alone, and control group. The PFMT alone arm is compared with a control group that presumably received no active treatment, fitting PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT but intervention is acupressure, not pelvic floor muscle training. Does not meet PFMT intervention criterion.
RCT but the abstract suggests comparison of two active PFMT delivery modes (home-based vs supervised) without an inactive control arm. No PFMT vs inactive control comparison.
RCT with four arms including PFMT alone and no active treatment (placebo/imitation PFMT). Directly addresses PFMT vs inactive control in women with SUI.
Qualitative study (telephone interviews) embedded in an RCT of two PFMT delivery modes. Not a comparative effectiveness trial of PFMT vs inactive control.
Secondary analysis of a PFMT program cohort seeking predictors of success. Not a RCT comparing PFMT with an inactive control.
This is a Cochrane systematic review (not a primary study).
Narrative review article on exercise physiology, not a trial.
Descriptive anatomical article, not a trial.
Not a trial; describes the HSCL symptom inventory. Not relevant to PFMT for UI.
Chapter/overview on conservative management, not a primary trial.
Methodology article about intention-to-treat and post-randomisation exclusions, not a trial.
Cochrane review (not a primary study), and compares PFMT vs other active treatments, not inactive control.
Consensus/methodology article on outcome measures, not a trial.
Observational MRI cohort study nested within a quasi-experimental study; not a RCT of PFMT vs inactive control.

RCT but intervention is urodynamic investigation prior to conservative treatment; both arms received conservative treatment (physiotherapy and bladder retraining). No PFMT vs inactive control comparison.
Descriptive study of incontinence pathophysiology in institutionalised elderly; not a trial.
Cochrane review protocol/review on PFMT in antenatal/postnatal women. Not a primary trial.
